transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… my family says I needed to come in. They’re upset because I spent our savings on wood and lights and display things for the house.

I was just trying to get it done. I kept working after dark. It felt like if I stopped, the house… the whole block maybe… would miss its chance.
Have you needed less sleep lately, or felt that you could get by with less sleep than usual?
I don’t know… I haven’t really been keeping track of sleep. Maybe it’s been off some, but I can’t say for sure.
Have you been more active than usual, like starting a lot of projects or moving around a lot more?
Yeah… I guess I’ve been up more. I don’t sit in the chair much anymore. I keep going from the garden to the darkroom to the porch, carrying tools around, fixing things before anybody even asks.
Have you been feeling unusually happy, excited, or irritable lately?
I guess… yes. Most days I feel kind of charged up, almost good, like I’m younger again. But if my wife or the contractors start questioning me, I get hot pretty quick. I’ve yelled some.
How long have you been feeling this way — the increased energy, less need for sleep, and being more active than usual?
I suppose… about three months now. Since the remodeling started and the whole house got turned upside down.
Have you had periods where your mood was either unusually high, euphoric, or overly confident — like you were on top of the world — and this was different from your usual self?
Yeah… I guess so. Most days I feel kind of charged up, almost happy, like I’m young again. But then if my wife or those contractors start questioning me, I get hot fast… I’ve yelled.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports elevated mood, increased energy, irritability, and engagement in multiple projects over a period of about three months. These symptoms align with a manic episode, which supports F31.2 (Bipolar Disorder, Current Episode Manic). F31.1 (Bipolar Disorder, Current Episode Hypomanic) is ruled out as the symptoms appear to be more severe and have caused significant impairment.
